items.title: The first jazz recording
items.claim: The Original Dixieland Jass Band made what is widely cited as the first commercially released jazz record in February 1917. What is notable about the band's identity?

options.text: It consisted of New Orleans-based white musicians, recording before any African American jazz band
It was the original Louis Armstrong Hot Five

items.reveal_title: An all-white band recorded jazz before the Black originators
items.reveal:
Recording technology and the racially segregated music industry meant the Original Dixieland Jass Band reached commercial release first.

Joe 'King' Oliver, Kid Ory and others were performing earlier; many of their performances were never recorded.
items.why: The historical record of an art form can systematically misrepresent who created it.

items.title: Streaming payouts per stream
items.claim: Reported per-stream payouts from Spotify to rights holders in the early 2020s are roughly which range?
items.reveal_title: Fractions of a cent per stream
items.reveal:
Industry reports and Spotify's Loud and Clear site indicate average per-stream rates of about $0.003 to $0.005, with substantial variation between rights holders and territories.

From 2024 Spotify required tracks to reach 1,000 streams in 12 months before generating royalties at all.
items.why: The economics of recorded music differ fundamentally between physical and streaming eras.

items.title: When Vivaldi was rediscovered
items.claim: After Vivaldi's death in 1741 his music largely disappeared from concert programmes. When did serious revival begin?

options.text: Within ten years of his death
The 1920s-1950s, after manuscript discoveries in Turin

items.reveal:
Manuscripts found in monastic libraries reached the Biblioteca Nazionale di Torino in the 1920s-1930s. Recording, especially after 1950, restored Vivaldi to the canon.

The Four Seasons (1725) is now among the most recorded works in classical music.
items.why: Canonical status is reconstructed, not fixed; archival luck matters.
